subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph boundaries as in-band text, explicit boundary metadata, or an intentionally partial common-case text repair?
rationale: The bug and the common-case fix are clear, but the near-`maxChars` case requires choosing the durable streaming payload contract before a correct merge verdict is safe.

options.title: Require a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit boundary metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split seam metadata through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial repair
options.body: Maintainers could intentionally land the common-case separator fix while leaving the exact near-limit boundary documented as remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-`maxChars` splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has strong history across block coalescing, chunking hardening, and the affected streaming boundary.
